items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: They had an alto player that was later in my big band at Dunbar Palace College named John Williams.

ctx.x: -- high hat and all (inaudible), and they went that, -- but they had some great musicians in that band, if I remember correctly. They had a piano player that has been playing in the Village, down in the Village in New York a long time, named Don Frye. He was one of the original bands. I don't know if they call themselves The Syncopaters or not. I forgot, but they're out of -- they were out of Springfield, Ohio. Lloyd Scott was a drummer, and Cecil Scott was a saxophonist. They had an alto player that was later in…

They had a great trumpet player with them. They and you know him, (Bill Coleman - ed.) later went to Europe, (Inaudible) Johnson, Coleman Johnson, excellent trumpet player. He went to Europe. In fact, I think he's still in Europe. Then they had another trumpet player that took his place, great big guy. I know you know this guy's name. I'll get it back to you. But getting back to that band, Dickie Wells was in that group, and he always played a real weird style of trombone.
